name: Field_Placement_CellMatchesAtPoint
summary: Placement-grid predicate: resolves the cell that contains the point (x, y) inside the row rectangle at desc->row+0x30..+0x36 (0x0062CB64 returns y*width+x, or -1 outside), then compares that cell's state byte with the expected value in desc->expectedState (0x0062C23C). Returns 1 only when the point is inside the grid and the cell state matches. Used to accept or reject a candidate placement cell.
evidence: NEW: exact-address xref (the project xref.json attributes calls to the merged Ghidra symbol, which here spans 0x00642248..0x00642344 and swallowed six unrelated neighbours) gives five real callers, all field placement: Field_Placement_TestAreaA (0x006E4900, per-cell overlap test), Field_FindPlacementCellByDelta (0x003BC98C), maybe_Ui_List_MoveCursorToFreeCell (0x003BCCA8), maybe_Ui_List_CanMoveCursor (0x003BCC30) and maybe_Ui_Overlay_CheckEntryPlacement (0x0023AA5C). Disassembly of the two callees: 0x0062CB64 = 'cell index from point' over the s16 rect at +0x30..+0x36 (returns -1 when outside), 0x0062C23C = 'cell state byte == expected' (ldrb [base+4+rel+idx*2+1]). Field_Placement_TestAreaA builds the descriptor as {word, word, expectedState=1}, which is exactly the shape this function reads. The old 'Ui_List_' prefix described a menu cursor; the callers are the field placement grid.

name: maybe_Ui_Part_IsVisibleOrForced

Still no caller and no vtable slot, so the class and the 'visible' wording stay unproven.
evidence: NEW (negative): exact-address xref finds no direct caller at all - the eleven callers listed by xref.json belong to the six small accessors Ghidra merged into this 368-byte symbol (0x00642858 'kind == 4', 0x0064286C, 0x00642884, 0x0064288C, 0x00642894, 0x006428A0). Disassembly of the callee 0x00649BFC (a mid-entry of the 0x00649BD8 blob) is 'vldr s0,[r0,#0x2c]; vcmp s0, 0.0f; return != 0', so the middle test is a float compare at owner+0x148, not a boolean flag. That refines the summary but does not identify the class, so the maybe_ prefix stays.

name: maybe_Ui_Object_NotifyChild
summary: Two-step virtual forwarder: calls self->vtbl[+0x70](self) and tail-calls slot 2 (+0x08) on the object it returns. The direction is unproven - if +0x70 is an owner/parent getter the notification goes to the owner, not to a child, so the 'NotifyChild' wording is only a guess.
evidence: NEW (negative): exact-address xref finds no caller, and the address is not a slot in any of the four rodata tables, so nothing pins the class or the direction. Disassembly confirms the shape exactly: ldr r1,[r0]; ldr r1,[r1,#0x70]; blx r1; ldr r1,[r0]; ldr r1,[r1,#8]; bx r1 - a pure two-hop forwarder with no other work. The neighbouring rodata strings 'common_3d_up_joy.bflyt' / 'common_2d_up_joy.bflyt' at 0x00643704 place it in UI layout code, which is why the Ui_ prefix is kept, but 'child' versus 'owner' cannot be decided from this body.

The class is still only inferred from the +0x1F38/+0x1F60 offsets, so the maybe_ prefix stays.

name: Sound_SeqField_GetValue_Off08
summary: Reads the full type-1 word of the sub-table at rec+8 through 0x00661534, returning 0 when the field is absent.
evidence: NEW: the named caller Sound_Seq_GetWaveRefBase (0x006610B0, call at 0x006610D4) stores the result as outWaveRef[1], i.e. the second word of a wave reference, which is a full-word field read. The one-argument signature follows the same push {r3,lr} + add r0,r0,#8 pattern as its siblings.

name: Sound_SeqField_GetValue_Off0C
summary: Reads the full type-0 word of the sub-table at rec+0xC through 0x00661534, returning 0 when the field is absent.
evidence: NEW: the named caller Sound_Seq_GetTrackKindBase (0x006612B4, call at 0x006612E8) stores the result as *outTrackKind, the primary value of the track-kind query. The sub-table offset is +0xC (add r0,r0,#0xc) and the tag type is 0, matching the name.

name: Sound_SeqField_GetByte_Off0C
summary: Reads the low byte of the type-1 field in the sub-table at rec+0xC through 0x00661534, defaulting to 0x40 when the field is absent.
evidence: NEW: the named caller Sound_Seq_GetTrackKindBase (0x006612B4, call at 0x006612FC) stores the result as a byte in its output struct. The body is the +0xC twin of Sound_SeqField_GetByte_Off08 (same 0x40 default, same &0xff mask), which is exactly what the name says.

name: Sound_SeqField_GetFlag_Off0C
summary: Boolean accessor on the sub-table at rec+0xC: returns 0 when the field is absent or its high byte is zero, otherwise 1.
evidence: NEW: the named caller Sound_Seq_GetTrackKindBase (0x006612B4, call at 0x00661308) stores the result as a byte flag at +0x19 of its output struct, so the value really is consumed as a boolean. The body tests (value & 0xffff) >> 8, i.e. the high byte of the type-1 field at rec+0xC.

name: Sound_SeqField_GetInt_Off14
summary: Reads the type-0x1F integer of the sub-table at rec+0x14 through 0x00661534, returning 0xFFFFFFFF when the field is absent.
evidence: NEW: the caller maybe_Sound_Seq_GetTrackOffsetBase (0x00660D3C) tail-jumps straight into this function (b at 0x00660D54) after resolving the record, so this is the value that the timestamp path returns. The body reads rec+0x14 with tag 0x1F and substitutes 0xFFFFFFFF, matching the name exactly.

name: Sound_SeqField_GetPointer_Off14
summary: Resolves a type-8 relative pointer inside the sub-table at rec+0x14 (result = stored offset + rec, without the extra dereference of the type-9 variant), returning 0 when the field is absent.
evidence: NEW: the named caller Sound_Seq_GetEntryPairBase (0x00660CF0, call at 0x00660D08) dereferences the returned pointer and copies *p, p[1], p[2] and byte +9 into its output pair, so the result really is a pointer into the record. The body adds rec to the stored offset, which is the relative-pointer convention the name describes.

name: maybe_Sound_SeqField_GetPointerValueA
summary: Returns the first word of the sub-table reached from self+0x3C through the relative-offset resolver 0x0065FB98 (self->f_3C + *(u32*)(self->f_3C + 0x34)). One of three pointer-getter variants that differ only in which sub-table they resolve.
evidence: NEW: disassembly of 0x0065FB98 is 'ldr r1,[r0,#0x34]; add r0,r0,r1; bx lr', so variant A resolves the +0x34 sub-table; the siblings resolve +0x2C (B) and +0x1C (C). That makes the A/B/C naming meaningful, but no caller exists for any of the three, so what the first word means is still unknown. Kept as maybe_.

name: maybe_Sound_SeqField_NotifyChange
summary: If the sequence-field sub-object at self+0x3C resolves through 0x0065F678, calls the record-kind getter 0x0065FF20 and discards the result. The 'notify' wording is only the previous guess: the body is a resolve-then-query pair with no visible side effect.
evidence: NEW (negative): exact-address xref finds no caller. Disassembly of 0x0065FF20 is 'ldrh r0,[r0,#0xc]; sub r0,r0,#0x2200; subs r0,r0,#1; moveq r0,#2; ... moveq r0,#3; ... movne r0,#0', i.e. a pure tag-to-kind mapping with no side effect, so the second call cannot be a notification. The name is kept only because 'query the kind after resolving the record' has no better short description.

name: maybe_Sound_Seq_GetDataRange
signature: u32 maybe_Sound_Seq_GetDataRange(SoundSeqData* self, unsigned int id, unsigned int** out)
summary: Resolves the {pointer, length} range of a sequence entry: stores the entry id through out, then depending on the entry kind stores either the raw u32 at +8 (kind 0), clears the second word (kind 1) or reports failure (kind 2).
evidence: NEW: the single exact-address caller is maybe_Sound_SeqParam_GetRangePair (0x0065E030, call at 0x0065E044), which ORs this result with an extension virtual and treats it as a range pair - supporting the 'data range' reading. Both the caller and the kind resolvers (0x0065FE84 / 0x0065FEA8 / 0x0065FE58) are unnamed, so the maybe_ prefix stays.

name: maybe_Sound_SeqField_GetPointerValueB
summary: Second pointer-getter variant: returns the first word of the sub-table reached from self+0x3C through the relative-offset resolver 0x0065FBB0 (self->f_3C + *(u32*)(self->f_3C + 0x2C)).
evidence: NEW: disassembly of 0x0065FBB0 is 'ldr r1,[r0,#0x2c]; add r0,r0,r1; bx lr', so variant B resolves the +0x2C sub-table, distinct from A (+0x34) and C (+0x1C). No caller exists, so the meaning of the word stays unknown. Kept as maybe_.

name: maybe_Sound_Seq_GetTrackOffsetBase
summary: Base implementation of the timestamp query: resolves the record through 0x0065F678 and tail-jumps into Sound_SeqField_GetInt_Off14, so the caller receives the record's +0x14 integer (0xFFFFFFFF when absent).
evidence: NEW: the single exact-address caller is maybe_Sound_SeqParam_ApplyTimestamp (0x0065E190, call at 0x0065E1A0), which treats the result as a 64-bit track offset and forwards it to extension virtual +0x50 - that supports 'track offset'. Disassembly shows the tail jump (b 0x00660D54) into Sound_SeqField_GetInt_Off14, so the function is a thin wrapper and the old 'void' signature was wrong. The caller is itself a maybe_ name, so the prefix stays.

name: maybe_Sound_SeqField_GetPointerValueC
summary: Third pointer-getter variant: returns the first word of the sub-table reached from self+0x3C through the relative-offset resolver 0x0065FBC8 (self->f_3C + *(u32*)(self->f_3C + 0x1C)).
evidence: NEW: disassembly of 0x0065FBC8 is 'ldr r1,[r0,#0x1c]; add r0,r0,r1; bx lr', so variant C resolves the +0x1C sub-table, distinct from A (+0x34) and B (+0x2C). No caller exists, so the meaning of the word stays unknown. Kept as maybe_.
